bias_disclosure: Exploratory correlation over final test values that earlier rounds already read; no selection, training or model replay happened here.
observed_pattern: The arms with the highest measured Recall are not the ones with the highest L1 lift: the #256 arms reach lift 8.5 but an absolute L1 prefix carry of only 0.064-0.067.
The best arm (TIGER_mixed_rq_F0, 0.057278/0.057226) carries 0.15993 of validation targets in the same L1 prefix with 4151 distinct L2 prefixes and 0.257 three-code collision.

The #256 lineage produces the finest SID (8840 distinct L2 prefixes, 0.0649 three-code collision, quantisation error 0.007673) i.e. an almost item-unique encoding, and that is exactly the configuration with the lowest Recall of the compared arms.
Therefore the binding constraint in this lineage is the granularity of the level-1 commitment, not the schedule of the curvature budget refresh.

r02_verdict.conclusion: Refreshing the maximal global module budget every 50 native epochs changed the final Recall by -0.00007, i.e. nothing measurable. The preregistered cadence hypothesis is falsified; the failure is located in the commitment granularity, not in the refresh schedule.
